# Results — Study 333 (Recovery-Speed) on a real survivor panel

*Generated by the package on the cached real tape. After each market-wide drawdown we
detect the trough and recovery date on the market proxy (SPY), score every name by how
much of its own peak-to-trough loss it had clawed back per day by the recovery bar
(its **recovery speed**), rank into quintiles, and hold a **market-neutral long
(fastest) / short (slowest)** book over a forward window — one execution lag (signal at
the recovery close earns the next bar onward). The headline pools the cross-section
**across four independent drawdowns** (2008-09, 2020, 2022, 2025); a single-event
reading is shown for contrast. As-of **2026-05-29** (the in-progress June bar dropped);
match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | 18 long-lived large-caps (current survivors — see survivorship note) |
| Market proxy | SPY (auto-adjusted, total-return proxy) |
| Window | 2004-01-02 → 2026-05-29 |
| Panel fingerprint | `51c5a3a1d9e4` |
| Drawdown events | 2009-03 (−55%), 2020-03 (−34%), 2022-10 (−24%), 2025-04 (−19%) |

## The headline — pooled across four drawdowns, market-neutral, gross

| Forward window | events | long mean | short mean | long−short | spread *t* | 95% bootstrap CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| 63 trading days | 4 | −1.6% | −4.4% | **+2.8%** | **+0.58** | [−6.3%, +12.1%] |
| **126 trading days** | 4 | +1.0% | −0.3% | **+1.3%** | **+0.23** | [−9.4%, +13.0%] |
| 252 trading days | 4 | −0.4% | −1.9% | **+1.5%** | **+0.13** | [−19.9%, +24.5%] |

- Pooling across four independent post-drawdown episodes, the fast-recoverers-minus-slow
  spread is **small and statistically indistinguishable from zero** at every horizon
  (|*t*| ≤ 0.58, every bootstrap CI straddles zero). **Recovery speed does not predict
  forward leadership.**

## Why one event looks "real" — the cherry-pick

Run the *single deepest* drawdown alone (the GFC, trough 2009-03-09) at the 126-day
window and the same engine prints:

| Sample | long−short (mkt-neutral) | spread *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **GFC only** (1 event) | **+22.7%** | **+2.78** |
| Pooled (4 events) | +1.3% | +0.23 |

One episode clears the bar; four episodes do not. A *t* = +2.78 on a single event with
three names per leg is exactly the selection artefact the desk warns about — the deepest
drawdown is also the one with the most idiosyncratic dispersion to mine. Reporting it
alone would be data-snooping.

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep (pooled, 126-day, market-neutral, net)

| round-trip cost (one-way × NAV, both legs) + 50 bps/yr borrow | net long−short |
|---|--:|
| 0 bps | +1.1% |
| 5 bps | +0.9% |
| 10 bps | +0.7% |
| 20 bps | +0.3% |

The gross spread is already inside the noise, so the net number is meaningless as an
edge — costs are not even the binding constraint here; the signal isn't there to begin
with.

## Survivorship — and which way it points

The 18-name universe is a set of **current survivors** projected backwards. This biases
the result **in favour** of the claim: the names that drew down and *never* recovered
(the true slow-recoverers) were delisted and are absent, so the "short slow recoverers"
leg never sees the worst cases. The honest cross-section, if it included the dead, would
be **weaker**, not stronger. Even with the bias working for it, the pooled effect is
zero — so the conclusion is robust to the direction of the bias.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

On a deterministic synthetic panel the same engine recovers the planted effect **only
when recovery speed is genuinely coupled to forward returns**, confirming the pipeline
can bank a real recovery-momentum signal (and is a coin when there is none):

| Planted `recovery_edge` | long−short | spread *t* | shuffle-null *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0000 (null) | +3.9% | +0.97 | 0.203 |
| 0.0015 (control) | +19.1% | **+3.30** | **0.003** |

The shuffle-null permutes recovery-speed scores across names; the real ranking only
sits in the right tail when the edge is planted. The pipeline is honest — so the flat
real-tape result is a statement about the market, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Pooled across four drawdowns the fast-minus-slow recovery spread is
  +1.3% at 126 days, HAC/two-sample *t* = +0.23, bootstrap CI [−9.4%, +13.0%] — squarely
  in the noise. The lone GFC event (*t* = +2.78) is a single-episode cherry-pick.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no gross edge to charge costs against; the spread is
  inside its own bootstrap CI before a cent of cost or borrow.
- **A "fast recoverers keep leading" rule? — CHERRY-PICKED.** The effect exists only if
  you report the one drawdown that worked and ignore the other three — and only on a
  survivor universe that already stacks the deck in its favour.
